topic.title: The bank sold you the EMI, not the flat
topic.claim: A 25-year home loan doesn't make the flat affordable; it makes the EMI affordable, and that is the only number anyone shows you.
topic.moment: The builder's sales person punches numbers into a calculator and says 'sirf ₹48,000 a month'.

turn.believed: A longer loan is a relief because the monthly payment is smaller.
turn.actually: The longer tenure keeps the price high and you pay a big chunk more in interest over the years.

topic.feeling: I'll be paying for this flat till I'm almost retired.
topic.villain: Loan tenures stretched to fit high property prices
topic.because: Builders and banks both win when the conversation is about the monthly figure. The total cost is hidden behind a smaller, friendlier number.
topic.payoff: Ask for the total you will pay over the loan, not the EMI. Then decide.
topic.behaviour: Buyers pick the longest tenure to fit EMI within salary; sellers pitch only the EMI.
topic.mechanism: A smaller monthly number makes a high total price easy to say yes to.
topic.group: First-time homebuyers in their late 20s and early 30s
topic.send_to: The couple currently visiting sample flats on weekends.
topic.why_now: Flat prices keep rising, so tenures get longer to keep the EMI looking fine.
topic.needs_facts: A simple worked example: total interest paid on a typical home loan at current rates over 20 vs 25 years.

score.why: A long loan makes the EMI affordable, not the flat; it hits the weekend flat-visit couple.
